real_world.product: Boulton and Watt rotative steam engine of 1785 (Whitbread engine), Powerhouse Museum, Sydney
real_world.use: The beam's connecting rod carries a planet gear that orbits a sun gear on the flywheel shaft, turning the flywheel twice per stroke cycle without a crank.

real_world.product: Boulton and Watt 1785 engine, Powerhouse Museum, Sydney
real_world.use: The planet gear on the connecting rod rolls around the sun gear on the flywheel shaft to turn the beam's rocking into rotation.
A working model beam engine whose connecting rod drives a planet gear around a sun gear to turn the flywheel.
A triangular rotor orbits inside a transparent epitrochoid housing, so each combustion stroke is visible as the eccentric shaft turns.

real_world.product: Mazda rotary engine cutaway at the Detroit auto show
real_world.use: A cutaway Mazda rotary engine turning over shows the rotor orbiting in its housing and driving the eccentric shaft.

real_world.product: Toyota U660E / U760E six-speed automatic transaxle
real_world.use: The real Ravigneaux gear set with its two suns, long and short pinions on one carrier and a single ring is shown and handled as the heart of the gearbox.

real_world.product: Toyota 4A-C single overhead cam engine (1986 Corolla)
real_world.use: Cam lobes press the rocker arms, whose rollers or pads follow the lobe profile to open the valves in turn.
The grooved shift drum turns and its grooves slide the shift forks sideways to select gears.
A pin on the constantly turning drive disc enters the Maltese cross slots and steps the film sprocket one frame at a time.
A crank pin enters slots inside a cup-shaped wheel and steps the day wheel one position per turn, in the same direction as the crank.

real_world.product: CAMCO roller gear index drives on production machines
real_world.use: A ribbed cam on a constantly turning shaft steps a turret of rollers one station at a time and locks it between steps.
A globoidal cam on the input shaft engages rollers on the output turret to index it with a dwell between steps.
Each lever stroke drives a pawl against a toothed wheel to haul the load chain while a holding pawl stops it slipping back.
A finger on the hour wheel advances the date ring one tooth each day while a sprung jumper snaps it into place and holds it.
